name: product_type_conversion
description: Deals, win rate and won value per product type — the product shape (Bifold Door, Casement Window). Use for 'which products convert best', 'what do we win most on', 'which products are worth pushing', 'product performance', 'average job value by product'. TWO THINGS MUST BE SAID whenever you use this. First, a deal ticked with several products is counted under each, so the rows deliberately do not sum to the business total: answer 'how many deals' and 'how much did we win' from account_deals, account_won and account_won_value, which carry the real figures, and never by adding deals or won_value down the column. Second, quote pct_deals_with_product — deals with no product ticked are absent from these rows entirely, so at 70% coverage every rate here describes 70% of the pipeline, and because reps tend to tick products on deals they worked properly, the missing ones skew toward neglected deals and these win rates read a little high. Compare win rates rather than deal counts when ranking products. Say the deal count next to any rate; min_deals exists to set that floor deliberately. For the brand or material rather than the product shape, use product_system_conversion. A non-zero malformed_product_type means some deals carry an unexpected data shape and are excluded — mention it rather than ignoring it.

params.name: product
params.description: Narrow to one product type by name, e.g. bifold, casement.

params.name: min_deals
params.description: Only products with at least this many deals. Use to drop products too small for a win rate to mean anything — five is a reasonable floor.

params.name: win_rate_below_pct
params.description: Only products winning at or below this rate. Use for 'what are we losing on'.

params.name: min_won_value
params.description: Only products that have won at least this much.
